text_blocks.snippet: Recent scams active in Central Illinois include fake local business listings for home services, fraudulent government text messages, and local municipal or law enforcement impersonation.

text_blocks.snippet: Fake Local Business and Repair Scams

list.snippet: Garage Door Schemes: Con artists use fake online search listings pretending to be trusted local repair companies, arriving in unmarked vehicles and drastically inflating simple repair bills.
Storm Chasers: Door-to-door solicitors exploit recent severe weather and tornadoes by demanding large cash deposits, offering fake "free inspections," or failing to complete promised home repairs.

Fake DMV Texts: Scammers send fraudulent text messages claiming to be from the state motor vehicle or Secretary of State office, threatening license or registration suspension if an immediate online fine is not paid.
City Department Letters: Fraudsters mail fake invoices or notices using copied official city letterheads (such as in Pekin) targeting residents who recently dealt with local zoning or public boards.
Arrest Warrant Calls: Callers impersonate local sheriffs or law enforcement, falsely claiming victims have missed court or warrants that can only be cleared by sending Bitcoin or digital payments.
